data_fields.name: pet tier threshold (petpower)
data_fields.donor_constant: one row per pet type and petpower (highest row at or below the power is used)

data_fields.name: stat scale from power
data_fields.donor_constant: scale = power/100; HP and AC x (1+scale)

data_fields.name: size cap from scaling
data_fields.donor_constant: size x (1+scale/2), capped at 3 x base size

data_fields.name: charm break gate per buff tick
data_fields.donor_constant: 25 (percent chance to run the resist check)

data_fields.name: resist roll range
data_fields.donor_constant: 0 to 200 unless soft cap rule is on

data_fields.name: mount run speed
data_fields.donor_constant: mountspeed column of the horses row

best_idea: A companion's power is a number the caster brings; a data table picks the highest tier at or below it, and that same number scales the summoned NPC and adds a capped level bonus, saved with the companion so a recall keeps it.
decision_why: Keep the tier-table-plus-power shape for summoned companions as catalogue data; do not copy the donor's SQL or its level formula, whose cap comparison is non-monotonic (fixed in the sketch). Mounts and the charm-break roll are not adopted here.
acceptance: A server test at base level 1 asserts: power 0 gives level 1; power 25 gives level 3; power 250 gives level 11 (bonus capped at 10, added once); power 275 gives level 11.
